content: Nevertheless, this legislative amendment is poised to serve as a critical foundation for subsequent regulatory updates aimed at addressing emerging operational challenges and technological shifts in South Africa’s mining industry. Between 2020 and 2024, compliance monitoring and mining safety in South Africa evolved significantly, driven by a combination of government initiatives, regulatory updates, and necessary industry adaptations. During this period, the South African government launched a nationwide mining safety blitz designed to rigorously enforce compliance with existing safety regulations and comprehensively improve workplace conditions across various mining operations [40] . This initiative emphasized strict adherence to established rules and served as a direct government effort to strengthen compliance in the sector through heightened oversight [40] . Although detailed, time-specific data regarding the specific strategies and measurable outcomes of this safety blitz remain sparsely documented, the initiative underscores the DMRE's commitment to active compliance monitoring and enforcement practices. Furthermore, industry statistics and trends, such as those highlighted in ongoing discussions regarding 2024 mine health and safety statistics, reflect the overarching impact of these enforcement mechanisms on the sector's safety performance up to that year [29] . Collectively, these efforts indicate that South Africa’s mining safety compliance during the 2020-2024 period was heavily underpinned by government-led initiatives and broader regulatory shifts aimed at fostering structurally improved workplace safety environments. Looking toward the future of compliance monitoring, regulatory discussions have increasingly centered on the integration of advanced safety technologies. For instance, real-time personnel tracking has been cited as a critical necessity under Chapter 16 of the Mine Health and Safety Act, with requirements set for mandatory implementation by 2026 [32] . While this specific technological mandate does not directly inform the monitoring practices utilized between 2020 and 2024, it highlights the DMRE's trajectory toward highly digitized, real-time compliance oversight.
